question: Which landmark case first established the principle of judicial review in constitutional law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Marbury v. Madison (1803)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Marbury v. Madison (1803)** was a landmark decision by the Supreme Court of the United States that established the principle of **judicial review**.
 
• Judicial review allows the judiciary to review and invalidate laws or executive actions that are deemed unconstitutional, ensuring adherence to the Constitution.
 
• This case was presided over by Chief Justice **John Marshall**, who emphasized the judiciary's role as an independent arbiter of the Constitution.
 
• The case arose when William Marbury petitioned the Supreme Court to compel delivery of his commission as justice of the peace, which was denied by the incoming administration.
 
• The decision clarified the balance of powers among the legislative, executive, and judicial branches, solidifying the judiciary's authority as equal to other branches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:**

 
 
• Judicial review is the power of courts to assess whether laws and executive actions are consistent with the Constitution.
 
• It is a key feature of constitutional democracies and ensures the supremacy of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice John Marshall:**
 
 
• John Marshall served as the Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court from 1801 to 1835.
 
• He is widely regarded for strengthening the judiciary and establishing it as a co-equal branch of government.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Marbury v. Madison:**
 
 
• The case set a precedent for future rulings where courts could strike down unconstitutional laws.
 
• It ensured that the judiciary could serve as a check on legislative and executive power.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Supremacy:**
 
 
• The principle of judicial review reinforces the supremacy of the Constitution as the ultimate legal authority.
 
• It safeguards individual rights and prevents government overreach.
